program_meta.advisor_model: MIXED / MULTI-INSTITUTION, program-first at the MSc stage. Admission is to the DEPARTMENT-run M.Sc. program (Head of Examination Board: Prof. Dr. Matthias Hein; Study Coordinator: Heike Größl), not to a named advisor - there is no 'select an advisor' field in the ALMA application portal (confirmed from the full admission-and-application page text, which describes only the letter-of-motivation + CV + transcript + English-certificate documents, nothing about naming a supervisor). Thesis supervision is arranged AFTER enrollment, directly with individual faculty. Crucially, 'faculty who can supervise' is broader than the CS department roster: FAQ VERBATIM: 'The supervisor (Betreuer = Erstgutachter) of your thesis must be an authorized examiner for the ML Master's program. This includes all professors and lecturers at the WSI [Wilhelm Schickard Institute].' Faculty who are primarily MPI-IS or MPI-Biol.Cyb. researchers (e.g. Bernhard Schölkopf, Michael Black, Georg Martius as MPI directors) typically also hold a joint/honorary University of Tübingen professorship specifically so they can supervise WSI theses and lecture in the program - this dual-appointment structure is why MPI-based researchers appear reachable from the MSc even though their primary employment contract is with the Max Planck Society, not the university. Only the WSI Board of Examiners can confirm eligibility case-by-case ('If in doubt, please contact the Board of Examiners').
program_meta.ms_research_access: YES, structurally central to the program, not an add-on. The 4-semester M.Sc. curriculum includes a 'Praktikum ML' practical module and reserves time for a Master's thesis; students may also take a semester off (after 3rd semester, min. 72 credits) for an external research/industry internship. Because Tübingen's MSc ML sits inside the Cyber Valley / Tübingen AI Center / MPI ecosystem, MSc students commonly do their thesis inside an active MPI-IS, MPI-Biol.Cyb., or ELLIS Institute Tübingen lab under a jointly-appointed professor, which is a materially different level of active-research lab access than a typical terminal/professional Master's. IMPRS-IS (International Max Planck Research School for Intelligent Systems) itself is explicitly a SEPARATE, PhD-only pipeline (its own application/admission process, distinct from the MSc) - it should not be confused with the MSc: an MSc student can informally work inside an MPI lab for the thesis, but is not thereby enrolled in IMPRS-IS.
program_meta.notes: PREREQUISITE COURSEWORK MAPPING - FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED HERE PER INSTRUCTIONS: admission requires a transcript demonstrating (a) Mathematics: one- and multi-dimensional calculus, linear algebra, and either numerics or probability/stochastics, totalling AT LEAST 27 ECTS (Tübingen's own B.Sc. CS students earn 33 ECTS in this area out of 180 total), and (b) Computer Science: programming, algorithms and data structures, totalling AT LEAST 18 ECTS, of which AT LEAST 6 ECTS must specifically be algorithms/data structures. VERBATIM: 'Between 27 ECTS and 33 ECTS the level and content of the mathematics courses matter so please provide the corresponding descriptions of your math courses in your module handbook.' The FAQ is explicit that there is NO remediation path: 'I don't have all skills but missing X. Can I fulfill this by doing additional courses in Tuebingen ... ? No, we get many applications and we only accept applications which fulfill the formal requirements' and 'No, we only accept certificates from universities' (i.e. Coursera/edX substitutes are explicitly rejected). A minimum Bachelor's grade of 2.0 on the German scale (converted via the 'modified Bavarian formula') is also required - this changed for the 2026/2027 intake (previously less strict). Someone (not this pass, per task scope) must map Akshat's actual MIT Bengaluru transcript ECTS-equivalents against these two buckets before he applies. TÜBINGEN AI ECOSYSTEM STRUCTURE CLARIFIED: 'University of Tübingen CS/WSI', 'MPI for Intelligent Systems (MPI-IS)', 'MPI for Biological Cybernetics', 'Cyber Valley' (a state-funded innovation campus/joint venture, not a degree-granting body), 'Tübingen AI Center' (a BMBF-funded competence center coordinating the above, admin home for cross-institutional faculty like Andreas Geiger), the 'Excellence Cluster ML: New Perspectives for Science' (DFG-funded, houses groups like Jakob Macke's and the ML-Science-Colaboratory/mlcolab.org run by Fernando Perez-Cruz), and 'ELLIS Institute Tübingen' (a newer, partly overlapping PI institute) are FIVE administratively distinct but heavily cross-affiliated entities feeding the same physical campus and same pool of professors - all of them are reachable in principle from the M.Sc. ML program via joint WSI professorships, but IMPRS-IS (PhD-only) is the one genuinely separate, non-MSc-accessible track. Application portal is ALMA (opens ~February each year, live link only works once that window opens). Contact for program-specific questions: ml-master@inf.uni-tuebingen.de (use only after checking the program pages and FAQ first, per the site's own instruction).
